Katalog Berita (Halaman 51/57)

#1283. 32 Highest-Paid English Footballers in 2026 [Ranked]

Money makes the world go round. And that notion is particularly true for footballers, especially for those earning their corn in the Premier League, as they often take home jaw-dropping amounts of money each week. It has now become a construct that fans and pundits alike tend to converse about. Most notably, whether footballers deserve to be paid much more than their teammates is based on a string of factors.

The likes of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Ivan Toney have seen their weekly salaries rise dramatically since their moves to Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, and the Saudi Pro League respectively. But which Englishmen are receiving eyebrow-raising amounts of money each week? And who, rightly or wrongly, is being paid the most money of all English footballers on the planet?

A goalscoring sensation for Bournemouth, it was no surprise to see Tottenham Hotspur cough up a £60 million fee for the sharpshooting Dominic Solanke in the summer of 2024. Since, the Basingstoke-born striker – capped three times at international level – has scored 24 times for Spurs. Like many on this list, the centre-forward has had to contend with a number of injury issues.

Such problems have limited his influence for Ange Postecoglou, Thomas Frank, Igor Tudor and now Roberto De Zerbi. Irrespective of how many matches he's played, he still earns £140,000-per-week. On the international stage, Solanke faces the challenge of competing with Kane for a starting berth – and, as a result, his caps have been restricted to just three.

Tammy Abraham made his return to English football in January 2026 after five years away. The Chelsea academy product, who scored 25 league goals for Aston Villa in the 2018/19 season as they won promotion back to the Premier League, completed a £18m transfer to the Villans.

He's scored plenty of goals for the club before, but has netted just twice in the league so far in his second spell at Villa Park. Villa need him to step up and be counted following the departure of Ollie Watkins and many other key players.

Having developed through Villa's academy, the 25-year-old exited for Tyneside after failing to get regular game time at Villa Park. A fee of around £43million was enough for the Magpies to add the talented midfielder to their ranks, but he has failed to catch fire so far.

Wholesale squad changes, exits and a new manager, plus injury niggles have combined to leave him struggling to find the kind of momentum that saw him heralded as a potential future England star. There is plenty of work to be done for Ramsey, as he looks to settle, find his feet and justify the £150,000-per-week that he's currently contracted for.

Mason Mount, now of Manchester United, was much further down this list while playing for his boyhood club, Chelsea. The playmaker was signed by the Red Devils in the summer of 2023 and now receives a cool £150,000-per-week in Manchester. Only a handful of players at Old Trafford take home more than the injury-prone Englishman.

His first few years in Manchester have left a lot to be desired, though his progression has been halted by a string of fitness problems. Still just 27 years of age, Mount has recorded eight goals and two assists since making the intra-Premier League switch to the Theatre of Dreams.

Carrick's system is far more beneficial to him than previous managers, but getting into the team is still proving to be a difficult task. Bruno Fernandes essentially has his dream role, which won't be changing anytime soon. Still, across four competitions, if he stays fit there's chances to prove himself once again. Whether he's able to repay his weekly wage remains unknown.

There’s an awful lot of unjust discourse over Jordan Pickford’s position between the sticks for England, isn’t there? For years, Everton’s shot-stopper has been the nation’s first choice – and, well, he’s rarely put a glove wrong. Some supporters, however, are not as convinced about the talents of Pickford, who has racked up 93 appearances for the Three Lions.

For the Toffees, the 32-year-old has been equally integral. Albeit not the tallest of goalkeepers, his combination of shot-stopping and leadership is perfect for the Merseysiders. At the time of writing, the glovesman earns £150,000-per-week and, on a separate note, he’s Everton’s highest-earning asset and an undroppable figure at international level.

The last few years of Kalvin Phillips' career can hardly have gone as he would have expected. The defensive midfielder – who earns £150,000 every week – spent eight years with boyhood club Leeds United, rising to prominence in Marcelo Bielsa's system and style of play. Such was his form that it caught the eye of Pep Guardiola and Manchester City, who moved to sign him in 2022.

Despite his calibre, Phillips struggled to break into the City first team given that Rodri was ahead of him in the pecking order. Minimal minutes led to unsuccessful loan spells at West Ham United, Ipswich Town and Sheffield United. Despite his struggles, the Blades decided to take him on loan once again for the 2026/27 campaign.

There were times when big doubts came up about whether Luke Shaw was the man to start at left-back in the long term for Manchester United. He was regularly criticised by Jose Mourinho, but has since silenced his loudest critics with excellent performances that have made him the starting left-back for his club once more when fit.

Arguably the best English player at Old Trafford, injuries plagued his progress under Erik ten Hag throughout the 2023/24 campaign and the same followed under Ruben Amorim. Are his days at Old Trafford numbered? Perhaps, but he has found better form under Michael Carrick in recent times.

After the Poole-born defender signed a brand-new bumper contract in March 2024, Ben White has proven his innate versatility by playing out of his natural position. A centre-back by trade, the Englishman had previously nailed down a regular starting position for the Gunners – but as a full-back. His influence, of course, has waned in recent times, partly due to injury issues, and he is no longer top of the pecking order.

The 29-year-old, who pockets £150,000-per-week, took to his new role like a duck to water, but he's since been dislodged by Jurrien Timber. He might not offer the same creativity as the likes of Trent Alexander-Arnold, but when it comes to a mix of attacking and defending, there aren't many right-backs better in the league than a fit White.

Is Noni Madueke a player waiting to explode? Some would suggest so; some would suggest that his poor form for Chelsea was exactly what the 24-year-old winger can provide a Premier League side. Alas, Mikel Arteta and Arsenal saw him as a forward able to provide something different from a forward-thinking perspective – and the Londoner has performed well for the Gunners.

So far, despite not being a regular starter for the north Londoners, Madueke has been a constant thorn for defences up and down the country, but 11 goals in 55 Arsenal appearances suggest room for improvement. From a wages' perspective, he earns £160,000 per-week with the Gunners as a backup to Bukayo Saka.

#1282. Tottenham are proof that a truckload of NFL and Beyonce cash is no use if you don't spend it properly, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE - after Roberto De Zerbi's £500m team saw their mini-revival ended by Leeds

Published: 09:34 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 11:04 EDT, 7 November 2026

Clubs outside European football’s elite are convinced the game’s financial rules are rigged to protect the richest and keep out the pretenders.

But Tottenham are living proof that making a truckload of money from Beyonce concerts and NFL fixtures is no use if you do not spend it properly.

A decade ago, Spurs fans complained frequently that Daniel Levy would not loosen the purse strings. At the time, the club was riding high under Mauricio Pochettino but could not take the final jump that – perhaps – a world-class signing or two would have delivered.

On reflection, perhaps the hierarchy were right back then. Maybe if they had worked within tighter limits in recent years, they might have made more sensible decisions in the market.

Tottenham’s starting XI at Leeds cost the best part of £500million with Leeds’ barely a quarter of that. It did not stop substitute Noah Okafor settling a tight game late in the second half and ending Spurs’ mini-revival.

Consider Pochettino’s Tottenham side at its peak. We’re not talking just Harry Kane, but Mousa Dembele, Kyle Walker, Christian Eriksen and Danny Rose. Hugo Lloris, Jan Vertonghen, Toby Alderweireld, Dele Alli and Heung-min Son.

Not many of the current crop would make it anywhere that team which is rather worrying when we consider the sums Tottenham have invested.

Leeds United leapfrogged Tottenham into the top half of the Premier League table

Roberto De Zerbi saw his side's three-game winning run come to an end at Elland Road

The problem with this squad is that they have a whole heap of players in the ‘good-to-very good’ bracket, who are largely interchangeable among themselves. A few, like Micky van de Ven, James Maddison, Sandro Tonali and potentially Mateus Fernandes, are a little above that category. There is nobody, though, who you could truly call world class.

Take Roberto De Zerbi, too. A bright, talented boss who did commendable work at Sassuolo, Shakhtar Donetsk, Brighton and Marseille. He does not, however, belong to the top rank like Pep Guardiola, Luis Enrique, Unai Emery or – increasingly – Mikel Arteta.

Here, Okafor scored the only goal barely a minute after coming on, combining with fellow sub Harry Wilson and slotting beyond Antonin Kinsky. Leeds made most of the chances in the second half and ended a five-match run without a win, though James Trafford saved Jan Paul van Hecke’s header late on to preserve the points.

Spurs have enough talent to keep them well clear of relegation and it is the kind of squad who can make a strong cup run. That is what Spurs have often been in modern times and there is nothing essentially wrong with it. Given the cash the current regime have splashed, though, they may just expect a little more.

Every summer, they do it. They tweak, fiddle and fuss. They preach about high bars, mic up officials and apologise to angry managers.

They have even changed the name of their organisation from PGMOL to Pro Ref, but they will never remove the controversy that VAR causes nearly every weekend.

Towards the end of the first half, Mathys Tel screamed in pain after Jayden Bogle fouled him. Replays showed Bogle’s studs make a solid contact with the Frenchman’s ankle but after nearly five minutes of checking, referee John Brooks was told to stick with his original decision.

‘Jayden is one of the fairest players in the country,’ said Leeds boss Daniel Farke. ‘He is more like a butterfly than an eagle and he would not even foul a player on purpose, let alone injure them. It was never intentional and maybe this is why the VAR said it was not a red card.’

Bogle escaped because there was ‘a lack of speed going into the challenge’ which VAR Tony Harrington deemed ‘reckless’ rather than dangerous. Whatever it was, Tel was injured moments later and Leeds had got away with one. Tel will have scans and De Zerbi fears the worst.

In real time, it looked a standard foul. After re-watching, though, it was hard to see how Bogle could stay on the pitch.

For all the decisions VAR overturns correctly, there are still far too many that leave too many people baffled.

‘I can’t say more as I didn’t see the situation clearly but I was surprised to see Pedro Porro given a yellow card in the second half for a foul in a similar position,’ said De Zerbi. ‘I don’t know if [Bogle’s] foul should be a red card or not but today the parameters of the referee were not good enough for these situations.’

Leeds are planning to expand Elland Road, but the stadium must not lose its raw essence

Leeds are working to increase the size of Elland Road and hope that the capacity will eventually be 53,000. Whatever they do, they must not damage the place’s raw essence.

Only Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool have a better points-per-game record than Leeds since Daniel Farke became boss in 2023. The lunchtime kick-off will never match the floodlit fixture for atmosphere but the second half here was as raucous as on its best days, and the stadium shook when Okafor slotted the winner past Antonin Kinsky.

‘When you have a few games without the winning feeling, it’s always difficult,’ Farke admitted. ‘Heading into the international break, it’s important to win again.’

There is plenty to improve for Leeds. If Dominic Calvert-Lewin catches a cold, where do the goals come from? Who can replace what Ethan Ampadu provides in the centre of midfield?

These are questions for Farke to tackle but with Elland Road at his team’s back, he has solid foundations on which to build.

Leeds (3-5-2): Trafford 6; Justin 7, Elvedi 7, MUHAREMOVIC 8; Bogle 7 (Rodon 90+3), Longstaff 6 (Gruev 90+2), Ampadu 7, Tanaka 6 (Wilson 77), Gudmundsson 7 (Bard 46, 7); Calvert-Lewin 7, Nmecha 6 (Okafor 77).

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 7; Porro 6 (Gallagher 65, 6), Van Hecke 7, Van de Ven 7, Robertson 6; Fernandes 6 (Bentancur 65, 6), Tonali 7; Kudus 6 (Williams-Barnett 83), Gray 6, Tel 6 (Solanke 43, 6); Marmoush 5 (Kulusevski 65, 6).

Gennaro Gattuso returns to Naples as leader of Serie A. His Lazio side are still unbeaten after 10 games, with nine wins and a draw, and are top on 28 points. #1279. New Bromley boss Karl Robinson heaps praise on 'megastar' Jermain Defoe - with Premier League legend in talks over dugout return after walking out on Woking

Published: 08:00 EDT, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 13:33 EDT, 7 November 2026

New Bromley boss Karl Robinson has hailed Premier League 'megastar' Jermain Defoe as the ultimate professional following his abrupt departure from Woking.

Daily Mail Sport revealed on Tuesday that Defoe is in talks to join Robinson's backroom staff at League One strugglers Bromley after Andy Woodman's dismissal last month.

And while his appointment has yet to be confirmed, Robinson jumped at the chance to wax lyrical about Defoe at his inauguration on Thursday.

Bromley sit bottom of League One but their new boss believes Defoe's meticulous attention to detail would help the players find another gear.

'There's been a lot of talk but there always is with names like Jermain Defoe, who is a megastar. He's one of the greatest Premier League strikers of all time,' Robinson said.

'I have to raise and change the narrative of what this stands for,' the new boss pointed to the Bromley badge on his jumper.

Jermain Defoe is in talks to join League One strugglers Bromley as Karl Robinson's assistant

Former Salford City manager Robinson has hailed 'megastar' Defoe as the ultimate professional

'I have to bring people in to make me the best version of myself. I spoke to people who know Jermain and played with him.

'He was always first in. All the players who have played with him will tell you that. Steven Gerrard will tell you that.

'He was first in and still in the training ground at 4pm - massages, recovery, gym, video analysis of the players he's playing against.

'I was speaking to him about something completely different the other day and we were talking about discipline and professionalism.

'I said to him: "what do you do that for?". He went: "If I do everything right Monday to Friday and I play poorly, I can accept it because I've done everything in the week to be the best version of myself."

'I'm listening and I've got goose pimples on my arm. Then I'm thinking, that's probably why you're Jermain Defoe, because he did everything he possibly could to maximise his talent.

Defoe has been out of work since walking away from National League side Woking after just four months at the helm amid a strained relationship with the club's director of football.

The 44-year-old took charge of the final six games of last season and was expected to lead the club into the new campaign.

However, he failed to report for work on the eve of the season before contacting the club later that day to inform them he would not be returning.

The former England international and Tottenham Hotspur striker would add top-level experience to the dressing room, having scored 163 Premier League goals in 496 appearances - ranking 10th on the Premier League's scoring charts.

Robinson spoke as though he idolised Defoe when quizzed on his potential appointment, highlighting his humility and relentlessness as key assets to succeed as a coach.

'Failure isn't falling short, it's when you don't maximise your talent. And I think some of the players here haven't maximised their athletic, technical and tactical capabilities', Robinson added.

'For whatever reason, we need to find the key to what that is. I think someone like Jermain (would bring that) because he maximised everything he was and everything he is.

'That's almost the secret behind the genius of the top players. It's their attention to detail, professionalism and discipline – he does that over and over again.

'He's tried to manage in non-league as well. That, in itself, is dropping your ego to learn.'

Although Bromley are still working on finalising Defoe's appointment, he is expected to join Robinson in the dugout at Hayes Lane. The Ravens host Rotherham in the first round of the FA Cup this weekend as Robinson takes his first game in charge.

#1278. Carrick apology to United fans ominously similar to Solskjaer’s final match

There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

And that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

In that instance, United fans booed Solskjaer. Carrick at least received some polite applause from the fans, who are a smart bunch and know the club’s problems extend far beyond the man in the dugout. Still, it is always the manager who pays the price. Solskjaer said he knew at half-time he was toast and Carrick is now under real threat himself – and seemingly at loggerheads with his captain.

Fernandes’s criticism of United’s set-up and approach was cutting and a direct attack on his manager and backroom team. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” the United captain said.

Carrick has been telling us for weeks that he and his squad are together, that the team are not too far away, that it is all about small margins. He even described Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Leeds as a “fresh start”. But Como blew the lid off any pretence of that being the case. Even by the standards of this season to date, though, what unfolded here in the rain in Lombardy was shocking to witness.

Como, inspired by the outstanding Nico Paz, were every bit as good as United – who have won just two of 11 games this season – were a pitiful mess.

Having conceded after just 47 seconds to Atlético Madrid last week, United were behind after only 118 seconds this time. That in itself told you a lot about these players and this team and it set the tone for what was to follow: a masterclass in incompetence and indifference. There have only been four worse results in United’s European history, although you will struggle to find a poorer performance than this.

Neither looked sure of what they were supposed to be doing. There was just a giant hole where the attack should have been. Everything about them was slow, leaden. The confusion was contagious. United send both of their full-backs forward and it gives Cunha the space to get a shot away from just outside of the box, but his curled effort sails over.

There will be one minute of time added on at the end of this half.

Baturina is the latest to threaten Lammens’ goal. His strike from the edge of the box stings the Belgian’s gloves and Douvikas, who attempts to latch on to the rebound, is offside.

Penalty shout for Como! Douvikas is sent through and it looks as though Lammens is in trouble as he sticks out a leg over which the Greek tumbles, but replays show Lammens withdraws his outstretched limb in the nick of time.

There was also an offside in the build-up, so it does not matter anyway.

Milla and Perrone are really pulling the strings in Como’s midfield. The former comes from the Jose Bordalas/Getafe school of football (think Tony Pulis during peak Britannia era) but you would not guess it given the way he manipulates the ball.

This game has entered into something of a holding pattern, with Como retaining possession as United chase shadows, desperately trying to lock off the centre of the park.

Here, Coute inverts, picking up the ball in the inside right channels before spinning in a ball over the top for Douvikas to stride on to, but the Greece forward shanks his shot over the bar.

Thirty four minutes in and the first chants of “attack, attack, attack” can be heard from the United fans. There is currently a giant hole where you would expect United’s strikers to be. It’s so poor.

Lammens does well to get down smartly and keep out a Douvikas effort, speared towards the near post after a sweeping counter attack. The resulting corner fails to threaten United’s defensive unit.

Da Cunha, fresh off his first France call-up, has just sold Mazraoui a dream, spinning the Moroccan in the middle of the pitch before gliding upfield, sweeping the ball out to Valle on the left, whose cross is far too loopy to trouble Lammens.

For seemingly the first time in this match, one of United’s full-backs, Mazraoui, makes a darting run in behind. While the ball goes through to the goalkeeper, it’s the right sort of intent.

Paz escapes the vicious clutches of Santos, but bumps into Cunha’s outstretched leg and earns a foul near the halfway line. Santos, already on a yellow, will need to careful not to get caught doing anything untoward for the remaining 60 minutes of this match.

It’s hard to detect a game plan from United. Como look like they know what what they’ve been told to do but United are just all over the place. Andrey Santos will be grateful referee Sven Jablonski was lenient the first time he came through the back of Paz because he’s just scythed through him a second time minutes later and picked up a yellow.

That’s better from United. Cunha hits the by-line aggressively but his cross is cut out.

Paz then breaks away down the right and, sensing a lack of cover, Santos dives in and receives a yellow card for his troubles.

United string together perhaps their best sequence of the match, shifting the ball quickly from one side to the other, with Mount and Cunha combining, but the move breaks down when Tielemans’ attempted through-ball is cut out by Kempf.

Fernandes attempts to play in Tielemans between the lines but his pass is behind the Belgian and Como regain possession. It’s rinse and repeat moments later, but on the far side.

The detail on United’s passes has been so poor thus far, with Como picking up loose balls all over the pitch.

Penalty shout for Como! Da Cunha, Douvikas and Baturina combine expertly through the middle, trading the ball with cultured one-touch passes. Baturina is felled by Maguire inside United’s box just as he was gearing up to shoot, but neither the referee nor the VAR are minded to intervene. There is a touch, but it does seem very slight.

United have gone with the box midfield once more, with Fernandes rolling inside as a false 9. Como are counteracting United’s movements through Paz dropping in, so Carrick’s men are struggling to take control of the central zones.

Mbeumo bursts towards the by-line but Ramon gets back sharply to divert the ball behind for a corner, which is easily dealt with.

United drop into a deep block, forcing Como to build around the outside. The ball is worked to the adventurous Couto who loses his boot after an overzealous challenge from Cunha and he earns a free-kick for his troubles, but Da Cunha’s delivery fails to beat the first man.

Chance! Da Cunha plays a lovely through-ball into the right channel for Paz to gallop on to and he flashes the ball across the face of goal, but Maguire gets there before Douvikas and the ball is cleared.

United are struggling to string passes together as Paz cuts out a Lammens pass out from the back, but he cannot keep the ball in play.

United need to settle, and here they decide it best to keep hold of the ball for a while. There are a few sideways passes but the ball goes back to Como.

Valle makes a burst down the left and Dalot’s contact results in a foul, but the free-kick is not up to much.

Como 1 Manchester United 0 (Paz) Well, we said he was special! Como work the ball out to the right, with Da Cunha picking out Paz on the edge of the box. Neither of United’s centre-halves are minded to close the Argentine down, and he opens up his body before shaping the ball around Lammens and inside the far post. Golazo.

Michael Carrick has insisted there is not a “toxic culture” at Manchester United in the wake of scathing criticism from former manager Erik ten Hag of the Old Trafford hierarchy and player power at the club.

The current United manager – who is under pressure after the club’s worst start to a season for 40 years – also believes he has the backing of the United board, despite Ten Hag accusing Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos regime of a series of “broken promises”.

In an interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag blamed Ratcliffe and his executives for fuelling a “toxic culture” by giving power to players and failing to back him on disciplinary matters relating to Marcus Rashford, Jadon Sancho and other first-teamers.

But Carrick said he had not encountered any toxicity since taking over from Ruben Amorim in January and suggested United’s last two outings, a 1-1 draw against Leeds United and a 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid, underlined the camaraderie in the group.

“Since I came back, the players and the staff have given us everything that they could give,” Carrick said before Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Cesc Fàbregas’s Como in northern Italy, where he is battling an injury and illness crisis.

“We’ve had some good performances. We’ve had some performances that we want to do better and we can improve on. We’ve made some mistakes.

“But I have to say, the type of performance put into the weekend and for large parts against Atlético, there’s a lot of togetherness there. There’s a lot of will and determination to do better and wanting to do it for each other, which is important.”

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Manchester United’s trip to Como in the Champions League. Under normal circumstances, a visit to the idyllic Lombardy city would be a source of thrill and wonder, but Michael Carrick heads into the eye of a literal and proverbial storm at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia with his team desperately hoping to reverse their fortunes.

Two wins – against Ipswich Town and Sabah – in United’s first 10 matches of the season, a public outburst from Lisandro Martínez and accusations of a “toxic culture” at the club have piled pressure on Carrick. And an uninspiring draw at Elland Road on Sunday did little to settle the rising tide of discontent within the United fanbase.

When asked for his team news, the first words that came from the United head coach’s mouth were: “Right, bit of mixed bag to be honest.” That was not a great sign, and Carrick will be without Martínez, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Ayden Heaven, Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu, who are injured, while Leny Yoro serves a suspension following his red card against Atlético Madrid.

Like United, the hosts are without a handful of key players, with Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Assane Diao and Jesus Rodriguez missing from the match-day squad. The abundantly talented Argentine No 10 Nico Paz will feature, however, and he will be keen to showcase his talents in the Champions League.

Como have ascended from Serie B to Europe’s top table in three seasons (and from bankruptcy in nine) under Cesc Fàbregas’ watchful eye. The Spaniard is a minority owner and shareholder of the club, but as head coach he has introduced an incisive, possession-based style of play which contains hints of the managerial greats under whom he played: Arsène Wenger, Pep Guardiola, José Mourinho, Vicente del Bosque, Antonio Conte etc.

Join us for all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s five Serie A games, as Napoli in crisis host leaders Lazio, Milan visit Genoa, there’s Monza-Atalanta, a massive Inter vs. Como clash, then Juventus away to Fiorentina.

All eyes on San Siro at 17.00 GMT (18.00 CET) for a huge Inter vs. Como Scudetto battle to fuel Cesc Fabregas ambition.

Finally, the bitter grudge match between Fiorentina and Juventus at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

Second half is underway in Naples as Lazio resume play.

Strong tackle gives Napoli the chance to break, they get the ball into the box but Lang sends a searching cross over Hojlund’s head and into empty space from the byline.

Napoli not committing the numbers into the box and it’s making it hard for them to fashion a genuine attempt on goal .

Lazio get another good counter-attacking chance as Isaksen drives the ball forward from his own half but gets it mixed up and gives away possession.

Napoli then have a counter attack of their own before Hojlund finds himself with plenty of space and time, about 10 yards from goal, and cannot even get his attempt on target, fluffing it completely. Bit of a let off for Lazio.

Sutalo down injured after appearing to have pulled a muscle, he is receiving treatment as the Biancocelesti hurriedly prepare a substitution by the looks of things…

#1276. Osmand proves he's no Honda Civic... and now he's ready to motor on for Celtic

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EDT, 7 November 2026

When Brendan Rodgers returns to Glasgow for a Q&A session next June, it would feel like a waste of time for him to be grilled on the exact reasons behind his team selection for matches which, by then, will have taken place almost two years ago.

Frankly, those assembled in the Royal Concert Hall that evening will have their mind on other matters.

Nonetheless, there remains a curiosity about why the Northern Irishman overlooked Callum Osmand at a time when Celtic were evidently crying out for a spark up front.

Rodgers, you may well remember, had spoken with great excitement about the club signing the player from Fulham a few weeks previously.

Sure, Osmand was only 19 at the time. He hadn't played a single minute of first-team football, either.

But as a combination of Daizen Maeda and the soon-to-depart Adam Idah failed to find the net across 210 minutes against Kairat Almaty, you couldn't help but wonder if the much-vaunted teenager stationed on the bench in both legs might have been worth a shot.

Despite Rodgers giving Osmand the big build up that summer, the forward didn't play a single minute prior to his abrupt departure at the end of October.

While that was clearly his prerogative, the impact Osmand has made across an injury-stricken year does suggest that it was an oversight.

Handed his debut as a substitute by Martin O'Neill against Falkirk soon after, Osmand scored a brilliant flashing header in the League Cup semi-final against Rangers before sustaining a serious hamstring tear against Midtjylland.

Only back in contention on the final day of the season after surgery, he set up Maeda and scored himself as Celtic clinched the title in dramatic fashion against Hearts.

Having been sidelined again with an ankle injury at the outset of this campaign, he's rebounded in some style. His goal and assist for Camilo Duran against Besiktas on Thursday came a couple of weeks after scoring twice in a 7-1 rout against the Tynecastle men in what was his first senior start.

Callum Osmand made an instant impression off the bench against Besiktas

After just 13 matches for Celtic, it may be a little too early to describe Osmand as a Ferrari. But a Honda Civic, he is most certainly not.

The beauty of the situation, from the club's perspective, is that the player hasn't even revved the engine as he sets out on his career path.

Osmand, who turns 21 as Kilmarnock visit today, looks first-team ready any time he's taken the field. Yet he's the first to admit that the game-time those injuries denied him stunted his development.

Provided there's a fair wind at his back, though, he's certain there's a lot more to come.

'I would say I'm nowhere near where I want to be personally,' he said.

'There's stuff I need to tidy up on, like decision-making and all this stuff.

'But I feel like the more games I play, the more I understand and the more I learn.

'So, on a personal note, that's what I'd want to do - just keep learning and keep understanding my role within the team and obviously the players you're playing with.

'I've still only played a handful of games, so it's tough learning. But I feel like when you get thrown in the deep end, it's the best way to learn. You learn more off the worst games than the good games.

'It's just as long as I can get better every game, that's all I really want to focus on.'

There's no doubt, though, that there are many moments when he looks the real deal.

For instance, his brilliant finish after Callum McGregor's square ball on Thursday, his first touch after coming off the bench.

'It was crazy,' he smiled. 'It's a surreal feeling when it's my first touch as well.

'I was a bit nervous that I'd shanked it, but no, I'm happy that I caught it nicely.'

One of his next involvements wasn't too bad, either. Motoring into space off the left flank, Osmand had to find the perfect weight and direction on the pass which would allow Camilo Duran to exploit a pocket of space and round the keeper. He could not have played it better.

Osmand has struck up a good understanding with fellow Celtic striker Camilo Duran

'I thought he was offside, to be honest,' he recalled of the moment in which Celtic moved 2-1 in front.

'I was looking at the bench saying 'Close?' and they were like, "Yeah, it's tight".

'But I know where he's going. He's such a sharp striker, so I know if I put that in the space, the keeper is not getting anywhere near it. He's a top, top player, so I can't fault him at all.'

With all due respect to Colby Donovan – also assured after coming off the bench – Thursday night will long be remembered for the belated contributions of Osmand and Duran, who scored three goals between them.

The Colombian began on the right flank, but moved infield once Kasper Hogh tired. The understanding Duran had with Osmand was clear throughout and ultimately proved the undoing of the Turks.

'He's unbelievable, a really top player,' Osmand said. 'You can just see even by the way he walks and the way he moves.

'I learn off him every day. He's an amazing guy. His English is really not great, but somehow we manage to talk to each other a lot.

'I think I find him quite a good friend of mine now.

'And although we might not speak many words, you can tell just by looking ... I don't know how to describe it. Like we talk to each other a lot. Maybe it's little words, but I feel like we get on really well. He's a great guy.'

Duran's finish at the second attempt to seal the victory later on felt hugely significant for all associated with Celtic.

It was precisely the kind of big win at the right moment which O'Neill and his embattled squad needed to blow away the storm clouds. On such moments, entire seasons can hinge and reputations are forged.

'For us, it felt like a must win, like that was our sort of mindset going into that,' Osmand said.

'I think the boys did amazing, so hopefully we just get some confidence and build on from this and that gives us confidence to play more free and take more risks.

'Sometimes when you're not as confident, it's tough to play the football you want to play.'

#1274. Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave new era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”

This was not as comfortable but still an impressive performance from this new and exciting team. Alysson, the Brazilian winger, was their man of the match.

Emery had warned his players of complacency against the Norwegian champions, but Villa took command from the start and were ahead after 23 minutes.

Ross Barkley scored twice against Fenerbahce last week and was in the right place again to head Ibrahim Mbaye’s corner past Arild Ostbo.

#1272. 'This club's not used to losing' - keeper Johnstone opens up on Celtic struggles

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EDT, 7 November 2026

Sam Johnstone has warned that Thursday's dramatic win over Besiktas must be seen as just the first step on Celtic's road to recovery.

The pulsating 3-2 triumph over the Turks came after Martin O'Neill's men had lost four straight matches in Europe with just three wins in the previous ten matches in all competitions.

As timely as the result was, the keeper believes there's a lot of hard work for the side to get through before anyone can talk about it being a turning point in what's been a trying season to this stage.

Asked if the spirit in the camp had been affected by a string of adverse results, Johnstone said: 'Of course it has. I think the results affect it.

'This club's not used to losing and we've probably lost too many games for this club.

'We all realise that, but we have to put things right in each game.

'The lads go out to win every game, so the camp's good.

'It was tough. We're honest players, we're honest people and honest with each other.

'You could see on Thursday night that the lads put a good fight in and got the result.'

Signed on loan from Wolves for the season, Johnstone was handed his chance by O'Neill only to drop out of the team following an indifferent display in the 3-0 loss at Ibrox on September 13.

Celtic goalkeeper is finding his feet in Scottish football after a difficult start

But having been selected ahead of Viljami Sinisalo in the past five matches, the former England goalkeeper believes he's steadily making progress.

'To get a run of games for any player, you find your rhythm,' Johnstone explained.

'It was a new club for me, a new team, so that takes probably a couple of games to get used to as well.

'I think I've got to get used to them (defenders), they've got to get used to me and that only happens through playing and through games. It's great to be in the team.

'It's good. I love playing. It's a great team to play in, a great club to play for and we keep taking it game by game. We go again on Sunday.'

Johnstone moved to Celtic at the start of a difficult period which saw the side struggle for consistency.

Adamant that he's never regretted moving up to Scotland for a minute, however, he added: 'The expectation, rightly so, for this place is to win games.

'Unfortunately, we hadn't quite met that expectation and the lads know that.

'Like I said, we try to win every game and put things right.

Celtic fought back for a much-needed Europa League victory against Besiktas

'It's brilliant to play for this club. The passion of the fans, good and bad. The standard of players on the pitch, day in, day out at training.

'When I came, I said I didn't have to think twice about coming here.'

Having heard so much about Celtic Park on the night of a big European win, the keeper was glad to finally witness it for himself.

'It was unbelievable to experience this place, rocking and get the win,' he reflected.

'It's a great feeling. It's great to play in front of and feel the passion of the fans. That does help the lads and drives the lads on.

'As you could see, there were times in the game where we struggled a little bit, but the lads dug in. It's never going to be easy.

'In the Europa League, you're playing top teams and, after last week's result as well, we were under a lot of pressure. The lads came up with the goods.

'We've still got a chance to qualify, and that's our aim, so we'll take the next game the same as any other game, that we go to win.'

#1271. Furious Tottenham set to complain to authorities after Jayden Bogle escapes red card in Leeds' 1-0 win at Elland Road

Published: 13:54 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 14:17 EDT, 7 November 2026

Tottenham are to issue a formal complaint over the decision not to show a red card to Leeds defender Jayden Bogle after his challenge on Mathys Tel at Elland Road.

Video replays showed Bogle catch the Spurs forward on the back of his left ankle in the first half of Saturday’s lunchtime kick off but despite a lengthy review by the VAR, referee Jon Brooks was not sent to the pitchside monitor.

Tel came back on but was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes and Leeds went on to win the game 1-0 through a Noel Okafor goal.

Spurs, who will lodge their protest with Pro Ref, may cite the red card shown to Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta in the previous Saturday’s clash at the Tottenham Stadium for his foul on Micky van de Ven.

On that occasion, referee Michael Oliver originally gave a yellow card but it was upgraded after a video assistant referee review.

Former Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann told BBC that the Leeds defender was ‘fortunate’ not to be dismissed.

Tel came back on but was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes and Leeds went on to win the game 1-0

Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for this foul on Micky van de Ven in the previous Saturday’s clash

‘Bogle's challenge meets the criteria for serious foul play as he endangers the safety of an opponent,’ Cann said. ‘He can consider himself lucky to still be on the pitch.’

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi was more critical of his own players afterwards, but did say of the decision: 'I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor.

'If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve.'

The decision will be reviewed by the Key Match Incidents Panel in the coming days. Mateta is serving a three-match suspension after the Football Association rejected Palace's appeal against his red card he received in their 2–0 defeat to Tottenham.

#1270. Serie A official line-ups: Genoa vs. Milan

Milan bring back Diego Moreira, Christian Pulisic and Luka Modric and hope to revive their fortunes against Daniele De Rossi’s Genoa, who are coming off three straight wins.

It kicks off at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris at 14.00 GMT (15.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s five Serie A games on the Liveblog.

It remains to be seen which version of Ruben Amorim’s team will turn up today, as they lurched from a 4-2 home defeat to Bologna to winning the Derby della Madonnina against Inter, to a 2-0 Europa League loss to Ferencvaros on Thursday.

That involved a lot of squad rotation, so players like Modric, Moreira, Pulisic and Mario Gila return to the starting XI, along with Mike Maignan, who was suspended for that match.

However, Strahinja Pavlovic, Fikayo Tomori, Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Pietro Terracciano and Alexis Saelemaekers are still out injured, so Sankhoun Diawara is again in central defence.

Yunus Musah becomes a left-back, while Alphadjo Cisse and Pulisic support Goncalo Ramos upfront in what the official website claims is a 4-4-1-1 formation.

Genoa had a dismal start to the season, but the club stuck with coach Daniele De Rossi and that decision is paying off with three wins in a row against Venezia, Juventus and Lecce.

In fact, they’ve won four of the last five rounds, stumbling only against Roma.

The treatment table has practically completely emptied out now, giving him a full squad to choose from.

Former Milan players Junior Messias and El Shaarawy are familiar faces, the Little Pharaoh on the bench, but Milutin Osmajic has made such a strong impact since the move from Preston North End, scoring four goals in nine Serie A appearances.

Genoa have not beaten Milan since a 2-1 at San Siro in March 2020, while the most recent home victory was over a decade ago, 3-0 in October 2016.

Milan: Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Musah; Moreira, Modric, Rabiot, Cisse; Pulisic; Ramos

#1269. Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner

Let’s cut to the chase. If there is any justice, sanity or logic in football then Harry Kane will win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London on Monday.

Arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z

“I’m lucky I can play with him and not so lucky I have to play against him,” Rice said, and that summed it up succinctly.

And that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”

Arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.

The only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.

Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.

It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.

“Unsere nummer neun,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.

Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.

Kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.

Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.

Some passages of play in the first half deserve analysis. Just to highlight how good Kane was. After an Arsenal corner, wastefully volleyed over by Riccardo Calafiori, Bayern countered and suddenly it was three on two. Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, had to do better than shoot weakly when picked out on the overlap. David Raya saved. That was a let-off.

But who sprung that counter? It was not Manuel Neuer, the Bayern goalkeeper, taking the goal-kick, but Kane, with his sharp thinking. And then Kane launched a superb pass from deep which Ismael Saibari should have dealt with better. It should have been another opportunity. Potentially a goal.

Lewis-Skelly with a no-touch turn in midfield but then he takes too long and Bischof wins the ball cleanly. Davies nutmegs Rice on the counter, but Madueke tracked back diligently to snuff out the danger. At the other end, Karl fouls Eze who has enjoyed a strong game, aside from his goal.

Karl and Diaz are on for Bayern, replacing Gnarby and Saibari. If anything that shifts Bayern up a gear. Arteta has also made a double change: Lewis-Skelly on for Guimaraes, and Gyokeres on for Havertz.

The more open and transitional this game has become, the less comfortable Arsenal have looked. I’m not surprised Arteta has taken off Guimarães, as they have been struggling in that midfield battle for much of this second half. It feels like Bayern have taken this game to a place that Arsenal did not quite want to go: lots of space, lots of running, lots of interchanging positions.

Laimer with a foul on Eze near the left-corner of the penalty area, so Arsenal have a free-kick in a promising position for a cross. Havertz, Konsa, Gabriel and Timber the targets.

Brilliant deliver from Odeegard, somehow Arsenal fail to apply the finishing touch from a few yards out.

Bayern then escape and stream forward on the break, and Laimer snaps a shot wide.

Arsenal looking a little shaken at the back after conceding the goal, but Raya is fouled from the corner which helps them clear their lines. Luis Diaz is about to come on for the home team.

Bayern Munich lead for the first time on the night. Kane with a short stutter, before sending Raya the wrong way and wrapping the shot into the back of the net with power.

Harry Kane, what a penalty 🥶 He scores in his TENTH consecutive Champions League game to give Bayern the lead 😳 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/4k4jPCQEWF

Laimer’s pull back deflected into the path of Harry Kane, and Timber had his arm raised as he slid in to make the block. The referee wasted no time to give the penalty, and there are few complaints. Kane with the chance to score a ninth penalty against Arsenal. Raya up against him.

Bruno Guimaraes and Odegaard with some silky touches to help Arsenal win a free-kick in midfield. Arteta has some of his subs warming up, though he has already used one with Saka going off early on.

Arsenal close to a second goal again, after neat football involving Guimaraes and Havertz to release Eze on the left, and Neuer stuck out a leg to help Bayern scramble the ball away. It would be a surprise if this finished 1-1.

That’s a few times in this game that Arsenal have been ripped open after all going forward for a corner. It’s very uncharacteristic for Arteta’s side, who are usually so solid in their defensive shape.

The game continues to be very open, but some of that is the quality on show from both teams. Will Arteta call off the dogs at some point and tell his players to sit off in a defensive shape, or will they keep swinging punches?

Now Raya makes a world-class save at the other end! Upamecano skipped through the Arsenal press and there was acres of space to exploit again. Gnabry stood up a cross to the back post and Raya made a point-black save from Saibari’s header. It looked like he had to score from six yards.

What a save from Neuer! Down low to keep out a Guimaraes header from the corner. He was reaching back to the goal-line and he plucked the ball up on to the bar.

Arsenal were then stretched on the counter, but Saibari was offside.

Kane almost produced another great through ball within 30 seconds of the restart, but Gabriel made an interception. Arsenal need Bruno Guimaraes to be on the ball, on a couple of occasions he has been caught in space when Bayern come forward.

Arsenal respond though, and Arsenal win a corner through Eze.

Tah replaces Kim at centre-back, so a like for like change.

Arteta will be very disappointed by how Bayern were able to find Kane free in the middle from a throw-in. Whether Konsa should have been higher or Madueke further across, it was too simple.

A high-wire act from both teams, who are pushing numbers forward with and without the ball. Lots of man-to-man duels all over the pitch, and when one is lost there is loads of space to exploit. It has made for an entertaining half, and 1-1 is a fair scoreline. Arsenal controlled the first 25 to 30 minutes, but Bayern have looked dangerous.

The bigger story for Arsenal is the thigh injury suffered by Saka. It would be very surprising to see him before the November international break, at best. He pulled up abruptly.

Lovely Bayern move, whenever they reach three or four passes against Arsenal’s man-to-man pressure they have runners flying forward. Gnabry takes on a shot from a tight angle, and it deflects behind for a corner. Raya does well to claim.

Alphonso Davies’ pace is causing Arsenal some problems, and now it is Bayern’s turn to have a corner. Arsenal have lost some of their control of the first 30 minutes, but still look dangerous themselves. Timber is fouled from the corner, Arsenal free-kick.

Odegaard with a poor pass in the middle of the park, but Konsa produced a tremendous block to stop Kane’s left-footed shot across Raya.

Within 10 seconds, Arsenal are at the edge of the Bayern box through Rice and they win a corner after Eze’s shot was blocked.

The corner is flicked to the back post, where Calafiori was inches away from scoring from six inches out. Close to Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

The game is stretched now and quite entertaining, a very different feel to Arsenal’s Premier League assignments. Konsa realised Arsenal were short of numbers and lunged in against Harry Kane, hacking him down at the expense of a booking. Rice and his team-mates recovered well against the counter in any case.

Kane with another superb pass, perfectly curled around Timber into the path of Alphonso Davies who finishes beyond Raya. Kane had too much space in the middle of the pitch, Madueke perhaps guilty of not narrowing in.

Kane has played some absolutely absurd passes in this first half and that was the best yet. Alphonso Davies is so quick that Arsenal were never going to catch him, and the pass was so good that David Raya could not come to it.

A word of warning for Arsenal is that Kompany has Lennart Karl and Luis Diaz sat on his bench. At least one of those attackers will be on at half-time unless something changes.

Arsenal winning most of the aerial battles and duels for second balls at the moment, Bayern not building any pressure or fluency. There has been the odd flash of danger when Kane flips a pass in behind but Arteta’s team are comfortable at the moment.

Odegaard almost finds Eze with a lovely disguised through ball.

There was a 30-second flurry from kick-off where Bayern had Arsenal’s penalty area under siege, but Arsenal have controlled the game well since and they have another corner. Odegaard has enjoyed the extra space on offer all game. Arsenal’s captain whips the corner to the back post where Guimaraes was free, but he shins a volley wide.

That makes two goals in three games for Eze. Although he got hooked at half-time in one of them (against Forest on Sunday). It feels like that’s probably how it’s always going to be with a player like him, to be honest. Highs and lows.

Good work from Odgegaard in midfield, one lovely flick to help Arsenal restore some control.

Kane’s range of passing in evidence again, with a driven diagonal over Gabriel’s head towards Saibari but he could not control the ball that was fizzed towards him. Kane is drifting towards the left to open up the pitch for those crossfield passes.

Arsenal caught out on the break by Harry Kane taking a goal kick, from which he picked out Davies with a raking pass down the left. Saibari helped the ball on for Gnabry who was free on the right, but Raya was down quickly to save and Rice cleared.

Arsenal have a corner, after a nice Madueke backheel released Timber. They have the upper hand in this game, but they have lost a major attacking reference with Saka going off. Arsenal enjoying the lion’s share of possession so far, which is perhaps a reflection of Bayern’s absentees. Kane has just dropped into his own box to receive a pass, and Konsa followed him all the way.

Alphonso Davies runs beyond the Arsenal defence for the first time in the game after Gnabry dribbles past Madueke, but Gabriel made a good challenge from the wrong side.

Ezri Konsa just followed Harry Kane all the way into the Bayern penalty area. Kane loves to drop deep and Arsenal have clearly decided to stick on him, no matter where he goes. For a few moments, Kane was the deepest Bayern player and Konsa was the most advanced Arsenal player.

Havertz has been booked for a foul on Stanisic. Bayern have not been able to build a head of steam as an attacking force so far, but their pressing has forced Arsenal into longer balls forward. No serious chance so far.

So it is now Madueke on the right and Eze on the left for Arsenal. A shame for the spectacle that neither Saka nor Olise are on the pitch, and the Arsenal man had started the game quite brightly.

Saka had a quick chat with Arteta before going down the tunnel. He gestured towards his left quad.

Big problem here for Arsenal: Bukayo Saka has collapsed to the turf after playing a pass, and he looks to have pulled a muscle in his thigh. That is surely his race run tonight, and it looks like he could be out for a few months based on how he went down. Eze is coming on.

The Arsenal fans high up in the Allianz Arena are singing Saka's name as he hobbles off the pitch. He looks very, very uncomfortable. Eze is coming on, so Madueke will move to the right.

Saibari with a cheap loss of possession in midfield, allowing Saka to go straight at the heart of the Bayern defence. Kim players a good switch of play to Laimer, but Calafiori and Rice snuff out any danger and Guimaraes does well to win a midfield foul.

Arsenal get the game under way, playing in their navy away kit.

The rain continues to lash down. Jurgen Klopp, Germany’s manager, is in the stands having a flim-flam with Rafael Benitez, who has dashed to Bavaria from Anfield where he watched Liverpool vs Villarreal last night.

It seems like Vincent Kompany may have taken a leaf out of Thomas Tuchel’s tactical book. Kompany appears to have done the same here with Davies, usually a left-back, starting as a winger.

We are going to have to play I expect three or four different games at different stages throughout the game, so we need to have everybody ready to adapt throughout.

Kane has already played against Arsenal since leaving Spurs, so some of the vinegar has gone out of that sub-plot but it is still worth noting that he has scored 15 goals in 22 appearances against them. Several of those goals have been penalties, but Kane is so much more than a goalscorer these days, especially at Bayern where at times he appears to have a free role.

A fascinating aspect of tonight’s game is how Konsa and Gabriel decide to deal with him. Will Arsenal commit to a man-to-man press, with the centre-backs following Kane well beyond the halfway line, or preserve a more zonal approach?

Manchester United are now 4-0 down against a Como team managed by Cesc Fabregas. There is still 15 minutes or more to play. You can follow the rest of the game here to see if they can stem the bleeding.

Will the substitutes again make the difference for Arsenal tonight? In each of their last three league victories, they have won because of goals scored by substitutes. This speaks to the quality of Arteta’s squad, obviously, but also to the Arsenal manager’s ability to pick the right players for the right moments. Over the last year or so, this has become a real strength.

Karl had been expected to replace Olise on the right, but Kompany looks to have stiffened up his midfield by starting Pavlovic, Laimer and Bischof. It will be interesting to see how Saibari and Kane dovetail, two stick-on strikers. It is not Bayern’s strongest team, with Luis Diaz also on the bench.

Bayern Munich starting XI: Neuer, Stanisic, Kim Minjae, Upamecano, Davies, Pavlovic, Laimer, Bischof, Gnabry, Saibari, Kane

Subs: UIreich, Urbig, Ito, Tah, Brown, Luis Diaz, Boey, Sapoko Ndiaye, Karl, Binder

There was little doubt that Arteta would view this game as one that suits Jurrien Timber rather than Ben White. Arsenal’s manager has changed tack by starting Calafiori, who was rested for Arsenal’s first two Champions League games, but Bayern at the Allianz is a significant step up in grade. Madueke rewarded for his showing at Forest.

Arsenal XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard; Saka, Havertz, Madueke

🔵 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🟡 Two changes for tonight's test ✊

Vincent Kompany is in the building. It wasn’t clear whether the Bayern head coach would be able to attend tonight’s game because he’s been battling a nasty virus over the last few days. He did not do the usual pre-match press conference yesterday but clearly feels well enough to be here tonight.

In an extract from Sam Dean’s new book on Arsenal’s resurgence under the Spaniard, he reveals that Mike Ashley was keen to bring Arteta to Newcastle United in 2019.

Sam writes: “Arteta also did not have a coaching staff assembled. It is believed that he tried to bring some key individuals on board, such was his interest in accepting Newcastle’s offer, but that the timing was not right for the people he truly wanted. In the end, much to the frustration of Newcastle and Ashley, he said no.”

Arsenal: The Inside Story of Arsenal’s Rebirth Under Mikel Arteta (Pan Macmillan, RRP £22).

This is a proper heavyweight clash but, sadly for the neutrals watching, Bayern are missing some big players. Michael Olise is suspended, Jamal Musiala is injured and Joshua Kimmich is unavailable following the death of his father.

This should all work in Arsenal’s favour, and Mikel Arteta will be looking for a repeat of the energy and quality that his team showed against Bayern last season. Arsenal won 3-1 at the Emirates in November in a performance of real class. It was arguably their most complete showing of the entire campaign.

Ice cold from Martinelli 🥶 https://t.co/uQEHb4x7eH

Some excellent, if disquieting, detail from Sam Dean in this piece about the mood around Arsenal away from the first-team following the news of 60 planned redundancies. Sam writes that there are expecting to be other experienced and influential figures departing. The timing of cuts invites particular scrutiny, coming after the emotional peak of winning the league, record revenues and Mikel Arteta’s new contract.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

Why Maresca is sticking with Donnarumma despite Leipzig horror show

#1266. A death sentence for ‘sloppy’ cancers

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Lorenzo Valcanover is in the Division of Oncogenomics, Oncode Institute, the Netherlands Cancer Institute, Amsterdam 1066 CX, the Netherlands.

Reuven Agami is in the Division of Oncogenomics, Oncode Institute, the Netherlands Cancer Institute, Amsterdam 1066 CX, the Netherlands, and the Department of Genetics, Erasmus University Rotterdam, the Netherlands.

Identifying cellular properties that distinguish a cancer from healthy tissue is a crucial step for developing efficient treatments. One such characteristic is the ‘sloppy’ way in which some cancer cells implement translation — the process by which proteins are made from messenger RNA by protein complexes called ribosomes. This process can go awry. Writing in Nature, Wang et al.1 reveal a cancer-specific mechanism by which translation loses its normal ‘track’ of how it reads an mRNA sequence to encode the expected amino acids, resulting in a phenomenon called frameshifting. This generates proteins that have a distinct sequence of amino acids that are not usually made, and the authors show that this abnormality might be exploited for therapeutic purposes.

#1265. Bournemouth thrash Milan to seal greatest win in club’s history

Eighteen years ago, Bournemouth were minutes away from being liquidated and playing in the fourth tier. On Thursday night, Bournemouth not only welcomed AC Milan in Europe; they did so as favourites, and then pummelled them.

When Amine Adli curled in an 84-minute free-kick with his left foot at the Vitality Stadium, it put the seal on the most extraordinary evening in Bournemouth’s history. On a brutally windy and wet night, Bournemouth trounced AC Milan 3-0.

Amine Adli with a SUPERB free-kick to give Bournemouth a 3-0 lead vs AC Milan 🚀 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/KX5i5oM3TG

Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.
